§5 has zero practice questions. All four subsections (5.1 How the pieces fit together, 5.2 The master cheatsheet, 5.3 Top gotchas of G1, 5.4 The bridge) contain no `<details class="sol">` blocks at all (g1_s5.html: sol=0, practice=0), against the contract's "End each h3 topic with 1–3 practice questions in .ex boxes with <details class="sol"> answers." This is the worst place for the gap: §5 is the only synthesis section, so the note has no mixed-review problem set anywhere — every practice item in §§1–4 sits directly under the subsection whose single tool it exercises, which means the reader is never once asked to *choose* a tool without being told which one. Correct looks like: 4–6 problems at the end of §5 that deliberately mix chains (e.g. a counting problem that ends in a Bayes update; a tree problem where the partition must be discovered; an "is this independent?" item whose answer requires the L04 conditional-uniformity trick), each with a hidden solution that names which cheatsheet row it used.

Systemic ambiguity: "§1.x" is used to mean both the Bertsekas–Tsitsiklis section and this note's own subsection, with identical syntax and no disambiguator. In g1_s1.html "§1.2" appears 16 times, sometimes meaning the note's own §1.2 ("monotonicity (§1.2, property 3)", "finite additivity (the k-set property proved in §1.2)") and sometimes the book ("§1.2, 'Some Properties of Probability Laws', p. 14"; "§1.2, p. 13"). Meanwhile g1_s1 cites "§1.5" for its own countable-additivity subsection while g1_s3 cites "§1.5" ten times meaning the book's Independence chapter, and g1_s4 cites "§1.2" and "§1.6" meaning the book while the note's own §1.2/§4.x exist. A reader following "(§1.4)" or "(§1.5)" lands in the wrong place roughly half the time. Correct: reserve bare "§N.k" for the note's own headings and prefix every book citation, e.g. "B&T §1.5" or "text §1.5", uniformly across all six fragments.

Broken cross-reference at the head of §3.3 (g1_s3.html line 247): "Conditional probabilities form a legitimate probability law: $\mathbf{P}(\cdot\mid C)$ satisfies the three axioms on $\Omega$ (§1.4)." This fact is proved in this note at §2.1 (the `thm` box "Property (conditional probabilities are a probability law)"), and in the book at §1.3. The note's §1.4 is "Continuous models: probability = area" and the book's §1.4 is Total Probability/Bayes — neither contains the cited result. Since the whole of §3.3 (conditional independence) is built on this property, the pointer needs to be right: it should read "(§2.1)".

Garbled justification clause in the §2.2 chain-rule induction (g1_s2.html line 172): "Every intermediate intersection has positive probability because it contains $\bigcap_{i=1}^{n-1}A_i$… more precisely, is contained in none smaller than it; the hypothesis … together with monotonicity makes each conditioning event positive." The sentence contradicts itself mid-stream ("contains" then "is contained in") and reads as an unfinished edit; the contract requires "one clause of justification" per nontrivial step. The correct statement is simply: each partial intersection $\bigcap_{i=1}^{m}A_i$ for $m\le n-1$ *contains* $\bigcap_{i=1}^{n-1}A_i$, so by monotonicity $\mathbf{P}(\bigcap_{i=1}^{m}A_i)\ge\mathbf{P}(\bigcap_{i=1}^{n-1}A_i)>0$.

Two citation errors in §2.3. (a) The theorem box (g1_s2.html line 203) reads "Theorem (total probability; L02 slide 7, §1.3)", but in Bertsekas–Tsitsiklis the Total Probability Theorem is §1.4, not §1.3 — and §5.2's cheatsheet row for the same theorem correctly cites "§1.4", so the two fragments disagree with each other. (b) Line 215 justifies the countably-infinite partition case with "(using countable additivity, L01 slide 7, axiom 3′)", but §1.5 of this note establishes that countable additivity appears on L01 slide 11; slide 7 carries only the two-set Axiom 3, and the symbol "axiom 3′" is introduced nowhere in the note.

§4's intro and §4.7's title both misdescribe the recitation coverage. The opening paragraph says "Recitation 4 then stress-tests the toolbox on four classics: the birthday problem, non-attacking rooks, the hypergeometric urn, and the multinomial coefficient" — rec04 has five problems (P5, multinomial probabilities, is omitted from the list). And §4.7 is titled "Recitation 4 problems, fully solved" but contains only P1–P3; P4 is Example 4.9 and P5 is Example 4.11, both back in §4.6. A reader using the sidebar to find rec04 P4/P5 will not find them. Either move P4/P5 under §4.7 or retitle it (e.g. "§4.7 Recitation 4: the three probability problems") and add a pointer line naming where P4 and P5 were solved.

Three colliding numbered series inside §1: Example 1.1–1.6, Practice 1.1–1.14, and Problem 1.1–1.5 all coexist, so "1.3" alone denotes three different boxes (Example 1.3 = the four grid probabilities, Practice 1.3 = the 0.5/0.4/0.1 inclusion–exclusion drill, Problem 1.3 = the loaded die). The text already relies on the reader disambiguating by prefix ("Practice 1.4 gives |D| = 9 − 4 = 5"; "Use the continuity property (Problem 1.5a)"; "the loaded die of rec01 P3 (§1.7)"). Renumber the recitation series as R1.1–R1.5 (or fold them into the Example series) so no two boxes in a section share a number.

Practice 3.3b's hidden solution does not answer the question it asks. The prompt is "Show that A and B are conditionally independent given C = A∪B only if something degenerate happens — specifically, compute all three conditional probabilities for P(A)=P(B)=0.5 and decide." The solution computes only the single numeric case (2/3, 2/3, 1/3, product 4/9 ≠ 1/3) and then asserts "Conditioning on a union of the events is never innocent" — a general claim never proved and in fact false at the boundary: with P(A)=a, P(B)=b independent, P(A∩B|C)=ab/(a+b−ab) and P(A|C)P(B|C)=ab/(a+b−ab)², which are equal exactly when a+b−ab=1, i.e. (1−a)(1−b)=0, i.e. a=1 or b=1. Either drop the "only if" framing from the prompt, or have the solution carry the symbolic computation through to the characterization "conditional independence given A∪B holds iff P(A)=1 or P(B)=1", which is what "something degenerate" was pointing at.

Decision-guide subsections have neither an interpretation box nor practice questions, breaking the per-topic pattern the rest of the note keeps. §1.6 "Choosing the right law" has recipe + one gotcha but note=0, practice=0; §2.5 "Which tool? A decision guide" is identical (recipe + one gotcha, note=0, practice=0). Since these are exactly the subsections whose whole purpose is tool *selection*, they are the natural home for 2–3 "classify this problem, then solve it" items — mixed prompts where the reader must pick discrete-uniform vs area vs given-weights (§1.6) and multiplication vs total-probability vs Bayes (§2.5) before computing. §3.4 similarly carries a recipe and gotcha but no `note` interpretation box, the only h3 in §§1–4 with none.

The §5.2 "canonical worked answers of G1 … calibration points" table is incomplete relative to what the note itself flags as headline results. It omits Monty Hall (stick 1/3 vs switch 2/3), the chess tournament (P(win)=0.375, P(type 1|win)=0.4), Romeo & Juliet (7/16 = 0.4375) and the loaded die (4/9) — yet §0.2 advertises Monty Hall as the §2 hook, §2's summary box lists all four Monty numbers, and §1's summary box explicitly calls Romeo 7/16 and loaded die 4/9 "recitation headline numbers". A table presented as the master calibration list should contain every number the section summaries tell the reader to memorize.

§0's three subsections (0.1, 0.2, 0.3) contain no practice questions and no `<details class="sol">` boxes, against the contract's per-h3 requirement. §0.1 in particular introduces the model, the axioms and a five-step setup recipe, and its own gotcha box names three concrete modeling errors (non-exclusive outcomes, wrong granularity, assumed uniformity) — each of which is a ready-made 30-second diagnostic item ("here are four proposed sample spaces for this experiment; which are legal, and which support a uniform law?"). Without them the reader's first exercise is Practice 1.1, several screens later.

Practice numbering scheme is different in every section: §1 uses "Practice 1.1 … 1.14" (flat, section-wide), §2 uses "Practice 2.A … 2.H" (letters), §3 uses "Practice 3.1a/3.1b, 3.2a/3.2b, …" (subsection + letter), §4 uses "Practice 4.1.1, 4.1.2, 4.2.1, …" (section.subsection.index). Four schemes for one deliverable makes cross-referencing between sections impossible to do by pattern and makes the §5 synthesis unable to point back at specific drills. Pick one — §4's `<section>.<subsection>.<index>` is the only scheme that locates the item in the TOC — and apply it throughout.

rec02 and rec03 problems are reachable only by reading the body text; §1 and §4 give recitation problems their own numbered subsection (§1.7 "Recitation 1, solved in full", §4.7 "Recitation 4 problems, fully solved") and hence sidebar TOC entries, but rec02 P1–P4 are buried as Examples 2.2, 2.3, 2.4/2.6 and 2.7 and rec03 P1–P4 as Examples 3.2, 3.3, 3.6, 3.7, 3.12, 3.13, with no heading naming them. A student who wants to work rec03 before reading §3 has no navigational entry point. Either add a short "Recitation N problems solved here" index list under the §2 and §3 intros mapping each recitation problem to its example number, or mirror the §1.7/§4.7 structure.

Two practice items outrun the toolkit their subsection has built. (a) Practice 1.1(b), the second exercise in the note, asks for the count of tetrahedral triples with distinct entries and its solution uses the sequential product 4·3·2 — the basic counting principle, which is only stated and proved in §4.2, three sections later. (b) Practice 1.7(c) (P(XY ≤ 1/2) on the unit square) requires evaluating ∫₁ᐟ₂¹(1 − 1/(2x))dx = 1/2 − (1/2)ln 2, whereas §1.4 develops only polygon areas (triangles, rectangles) and every worked example in it is a triangle. Either flag these as stretch items, or supply the missing scaffolding inline (a one-line forward pointer to §4.2 for (a); an explicit "this one needs a logarithmic integral" note for (b)).

§3.6, Example 3.13 (rec03 P3 = Problem 1.31), part (d), the "Reading the numbers" paragraph: the odds-form cross-check is wrong twice over. It writes "the prior ratio 0.6/0.4=1.5" and "the posterior odds are the product 1.5×34.1=51.2 in favor of 1, i.e. P(S1|101)=51.2/52.2=0.9579 ✓". (i) The prior odds *in favour of 1* are P(S1)/P(S0)=0.4/0.6=2/3, not 1.5 — 1.5 is the prior odds in favour of 0, so it is being multiplied by a likelihood ratio pointing the other way. (ii) Even taking 51.2 at face value, 51.2/52.2=0.98084, not 0.9579, so the "✓" endorses an arithmetic identity that is false. Correct chain: prior odds (1 over 0) = 2/3; likelihood ratio = 0.081/0.002375 = 34.105; posterior odds = 22.737; P(S1|101) = 22.737/23.737 = 0.957871, which then genuinely matches the Bayes value 1-0.042129 computed two lines above. Note also that none of 1.5, 34.1, 51.2, 52.2 appears in computes/g1_s3.json (computes/g1_s3.py computes only ch_d_lik0/lik1/num/den/P_0_given_101), so this is a hand-computed number, violating the style contract's "NEVER hand-compute a numeric value". The §3.6 Recipe step 5 ("posterior odds = prior odds × likelihood ratio") points readers at this broken worked instance.

§5.3, Gotcha 2 (radar model), last clause: "the conversion factor P(A)/P(B) can be enormous when A is rare" is backwards. Bayes gives P(A|B)=P(B|A)·P(A)/P(B); when A is rare relative to B the factor P(A)/P(B) is *small* — here 0.05/0.1445=0.3426, which is precisely why the 0.99 detector reliability collapses to a 0.342561 posterior. Correct statement: the factor can be tiny (equivalently, the two conditionals can differ enormously) when A is rare.

§5.3, Gotcha 5 ("counting order inconsistently"), parenthetical example: "Mixing them (e.g. 6! over C(6,6)) silently multiplies your answer by a factorial." C(6,6)=1, so the expression is 720/1=720 — not a probability at all, and not the stated answer times a factorial. No plausible student error produces this expression. A genuine mismatch for the six-different-rolls problem would be an unordered denominator such as the C(11,5)=462 multisets of six rolls against the ordered numerator 6!. Replace or delete the example.

§4.4, paragraph "Two immediate consequences": the chain "$\binom{5}{2} = 5!/(2!\,3!) = 20/2 = 10$" contains a false intermediate equality — 5!/(2!·3!) is 120/12, not 20/2. The 20/2 belongs to the next clause (2-permutation count 5·4=20 divided by 2!). Write $5!/(2!\,3!) = 120/12 = 10$, then the alternative 20/2 = 10.

§4.7, note "Interpretation — why the answer feels wrong": "That event involves only the n−1 pairs containing you and needs about 253 people for even odds." Solving 1-(364/365)^{n-1} > 1/2 gives n-1 = 253, i.e. 254 people present (253 *others*). Since the sentence's question is "how many people must be present", the number is 254; as written it is off by one and reads as if it were coincidentally the same 253 as C(23,2). Say "253 other people (254 present)".

§4.3: the L04-slide-3 [UNSOLVED EXAMPLE] "Number of ways of ordering n elements" is solved in a bare

labelled "(… — Example 4.4)" rather than in a

box, unlike Examples 4.1–4.3 which cover the other slide-3 blanks. Consequence: there is no example box numbered 4.4 anywhere in the fragment (boxes jump 4.3 → 4.5), and the style contract's rule "Every [UNSOLVED EXAMPLE] … solve COMPLETELY in an .ex box" is not met for this one. Same for the k-permutation derivation immediately after it.

Fig. 1.5 (notes/img/g1_s1_flowchart.png, §1.6) contradicts §1.5. The decision node reads "Is Ω finite or countable?" but has only two outgoing labels, "countable" and "continuous" — the *finite* case has no arrow at all. The "countable" branch then goes to "Are all outcomes equally likely? → yes → Discrete uniform law P(A) = |A|/|Ω|". For a countably infinite Ω that law does not exist: the note's own Gotcha at the end of §1.5 proves it ("if every P(n) = c, countable additivity gives P(Ω) = Σc, which is 0 if c = 0 and ∞ if c > 0 — never 1"), and Recipe step 2 immediately below the figure says "Finite → counting; countably infinite → a series". |Ω| is also undefined/infinite on that branch. The alt text repeats the error verbatim ("if countable ask whether outcomes are equally likely, leading to either the discrete uniform law P(A)=|A|/|Omega| or summing given masses"). Correct version: the node must split three ways — finite / countably infinite / continuous — and only the *finite* branch may reach P(A)=|A|/|Ω|; the countably-infinite branch must go to "sum the given masses (countable additivity)" with no equally-likely sub-branch.

§2.3, last line of the total-probability derivation (fragment g1_s2.html, after the Step 2 QED): "and (using countable additivity, L01 slide 7, axiom 3′) for a countably infinite partition" — miscitation, and self-contradictory with §1. Per transcripts/L01.md, slide 7 states only the two-set additivity axiom plus the bare remark "Axiom 3 needs strengthening"; countable additivity is introduced on L01 slide 11. The label "axiom 3′" comes from L02 slide 2, not L01 slide 7. §1.5 of these same notes cites it correctly as "L01 slide 11". Should read "(using countable additivity, L01 slide 11; L02 slide 2 axiom 3′)".

§0.1 Definition box, first bullet: mutual exclusivity is glossed as "exactly one outcome occurs; no two can occur together". "Exactly one occurs" is the conjunction of mutual exclusivity *and* collective exhaustiveness, not the definition of the first alone — and the very next parenthetical then re-states exhaustiveness separately, so the definition double-counts. §1.1 gets this right ("Mutually exclusive — at most one outcome can occur"; "Collectively exhaustive — at least one outcome occurs"; "Taken together: exactly one"). Fix §0 to "at most one outcome can occur".

§0.2 roadmap is incomplete relative to the assembled note. It presents G1 as exactly four topics (§1–§4) followed by "note G2", but the assembled note contains a fifth numbered section, g1_s5.html "§5 — Synthesis, cheatsheet, and the bridge to random variables" (id="g1-s5" is present in notes/01_probability_basics.html). The hedge in the following paragraph — "where a topic runs long it is split across two numbered sections" — is also false: no topic is split; §1↔g1_s1, §2↔g1_s2, §3↔g1_s3, §4↔g1_s4 are 1-to-1. Either add §5 to the roadmap list or delete the incorrect hedge.

§0.3 notation table is introduced as "the complete list used in G1" but is not complete: it omits the factorial n! and the multinomial coefficient n!/(n_1!⋯n_r!), both used throughout §4 (g1_s4.html contains frac{n!}{n_1!\,n_2!\cdots n_r!} etc.). It also declares the binomial coefficient as \binom{n}{k} while §4 writes it 22 times as {n \choose k}; same rendered glyph, but the table is then not the notation "used".

srcref line cites "L01 slides 3–4, 7, 9–11" but the body cites L01 slide 5 (Recipe step 1: "If the experiment has stages, a tree is usually the right picture (L01 slide 5)"), which is outside the declared range. Either widen the srcref to 3–5, 7, 9–11 or drop the inline slide-5 citation.

Practice 1.4 (§1.2) asks the reader to prove P(B ∩ A^c) = P(B) − P(A) for A ⊆ B "and use it to show P(A∪B) ≥ max{P(A), P(B)}", but the posted solution proves the second claim purely from monotonicity applied to A ⊆ A∪B and B ⊆ A∪B, never using the identity just established. Either restate the exercise ("and, separately, show…") or give the derivation that actually uses the identity (P(A∪B) − P(A) = P(B ∩ A^c) ≥ 0).

Example 1.5, Step 2 (§1.4): the displayed bound is asserted as "0 ≤ P(A) ≤ P(B_ε) = 4ε² for every ε > 0", but Step 1 established area(B_ε) = 4ε² only for ε ≤ 0.3 ("For all small ε (any ε ≤ 0.3) this box sits inside Ω"). For ε > 0.3 the box is clipped by Ω and P(B_ε ∩ Ω) < 4ε², so the equality in the display is false as quantified. The squeeze is unaffected — restrict the quantifier to 0 < ε ≤ 0.3, which is all the limit needs.

§2.2, paragraph after the general (n-event) multiplication rule: the positivity justification is garbled — "Every intermediate intersection has positive probability because it contains ⋂_{i=1}^{n-1}A_i… more precisely, is contained in none smaller than it". The clause after the ellipsis is not a mathematical statement. The correct argument is one line: for k ≤ n−1, ⋂_{i=1}^{k}A_i ⊇ ⋂_{i=1}^{n-1}A_i, so by monotonicity P(⋂_{i=1}^{k}A_i) ≥ P(⋂_{i=1}^{n-1}A_i) > 0, hence every conditioning event in the product is legitimate.

§2.1 Property box claims Q(A) = P(A|B) "satisfies the three axioms of L01 slide 7, so every theorem proved for probability laws applies verbatim", but item 3 verifies only two-set additivity. Since §1.5 explicitly *replaces* Axiom 3 by countable additivity as the official axiom list, the conditional law should be checked against that stronger axiom (the same one-line distributivity + division argument works for a sequence A_1, A_2, …). As written, the "applies verbatim" claim overreaches the proof given, and inherits nothing for the countably-infinite partitions used later in §2.3.

Contract violation (STYLE_CONTRACT "Worked problems & practice": "End each h3 topic with 1–3 practice questions in .ex boxes"). §2.5 "Which tool? A decision guide" ends with a Gotcha and no practice item. The same omission occurs at §1.6 "Choosing the right law — a decision procedure".
